title: Specific retry can resend non-failed promotional emails
reasoning: When --promo-id is provided, the command fetches any PromoEmail by id, unconditionally changes it to DRAFT, and enqueues send_promo_email_task. That bypasses the command's failed-email contract and can requeue already sent, scheduled, draft, or currently sending emails, causing duplicate sends or corrupting a user's intended state.
reproduction: Run python manage.py retry_failed_emails --promo-id <id-of-sent-or-scheduled-promo>. The command will set that promo to DRAFT and queue the send task even though it was not failed.
recommendation: Require promo.status == PromoEmail.FAILED before mutating or queuing a specific promo, and return a clear error or warning for other statuses unless an explicit force option is added.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for retry_failed_emails, and the dry-run branch displays the current status without asserting that non-failed statuses are rejected.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create PromoEmail records in SENT, SCHEDULED, SENDING, and DRAFT states, invoke retry_failed_emails --promo-id for each, and assert status is unchanged and send_promo_email_task.delay is not called.
minimumFixScope: Guard the --promo-id path in retry_failed_emails.py before line 31 so only FAILED promos can be retried.
